newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht surges further to new high offshore.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht surges further to new high offshore.

text.p: The Thai baht rallied to at least a 16-year high against the dollar early in the offshore market as foreign players continued scrambling for the currency to cover their short baht positions, dealers said.
The baht was quoted at 22.300/22.500 in early trade offshore compared with 22.800/23.000 late on Tuesday.
Dealers in Singapore said costly baht funding through the forward swap market and maturity of one-month forward contracts still forced offshore players to sell dollars for baht in the spot market.
"Tom/next and swap premiums keep rising. It's not a good idea to borrow baht in the swap market right now," said one dealer at a European bank in Singapore.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium rallied to 265/295 satangs per dollar in the offshore market from 150/180 late on Tuesday.
Offshore parties have been caught severely short of baht after the Bank of Thailand's decision to curb baht supply outside Thailand last month, dealers said.
The move was aimed at striking back at speculators who attacked the baht in mid-May.
In the domestic market, the baht steadied at 25.820/25.840 early, unchanged from late on Tuesday on sustained commercial demand for the dollar, dealers said.
The Bank of Thailand set the mid-rate at 25.76 per dollar against 25.77 on Tuesday.
The overnight interbank rate was steady at 12.00-13.00 percent against 12.75-13.00 late on Tuesday.
